title: The Fir Tree
summary: A small tree longs to grow tall while children and workers decide its fate.

sentences.text: Deep within the ancient forest, where the damp earth exhaled the rich scent of pine and moss, stood a little fir tree. Around him towered magnificent old trees, their massive trunks casting deep shadows across the forest floor. The golden sun shone down upon his needles, and the fresh morning air blew softly through his tender branches. Yet, despite such peaceful surroundings, the little tree was never truly content with his present life. He found no joy in the simple moments, preferring always to look forward to an imagined future. What he desired above all else was to grow very tall and strong like his neighbors.

Sometimes groups of children came wandering into the woods to play near the little tree. They would point at him and talk about how remarkably small he was, which made him feel a sharp pang of sadness. He cared nothing for the sweet songs of the forest birds or the warm, golden light of the afternoon sun. All he could visualize was a grand destiny waiting for him somewhere beyond the treeline. He longed only for the day when he would be cut down and taken away to a magnificent house. In his mind, that mysterious journey represented the true beginning of a meaningful existence.

Every single day in the big forest was full of vibrant green plants and pleasant, soothing sounds. The little tree had many companions who grew tall and sturdy all around him. Birds would frequently sit upon his delicate branches and sing sweet, melodic songs throughout the morning hours. The afternoon sun always provided a warm, gentle light that warmed his bark. Yet the little tree felt persistently melancholy because he wanted to tower over the landscape like the ancient giants. He refused to enjoy the present moment, choosing instead to chase distant illusions.

Instead of appreciating his quiet surroundings, he always looked toward the coming years with fierce anticipation. He imagined that a wonderful, sophisticated house must be waiting for him one day in the great human world. Not once did he pause to thank the earth for the moisture drawn up through his roots or the sky for the gentle rain. His heart was entirely set on a future he did not yet understand, ignoring the quiet beauty right beside him. By wishing his youth away, he drained all the actual sweetness from his daily life.

The winter season arrived quickly, bringing bitter cold air and a blanket of white snow to the quiet woods. Men came equipped with sharp tools to cut down the young, straight trees that stood scattered throughout the forest. When the woodsmen finally approached the area, they noticed the little fir tree almost immediately. His exceptionally straight shape and brilliant green color made him look remarkably special among the surrounding evergreens. A strong, electric emotion ran through his wooden body as the cold steel bit into his base. They lifted him carefully from the frozen soil and placed him into a vehicle to travel far away from home.

He felt a great wave of breathless excitement washing over him during the bumpy journey away from the forest. He was entirely sure that his long-held dreams of a grand, sophisticated life were finally coming true. The vehicle rattled down country roads, carrying him toward a destination he had imagined for so long. Though his roots were gone, he felt lighter than air, intoxicated by the promise of change. Not a single shadow of doubt clouded his optimistic mind as the landscape shifted from wild woods to human settlements.

The workers carried the little tree inside a large, imposing building with remarkably high ceilings and tall windows. They placed him securely in a corner of the main reception room, anchoring his base firmly in a wooden tub filled with sand. Many people worked together rapidly to prepare his branches for the special evening ahead. They hung glittering lights, painted ornaments, and sweet treats all over his trembling green needles. Children eventually rushed into the room with wide smiles and loud, ringing laughter that echoed off the walls. They played energetic games and danced joyfully while wonderful music played softly in the background.

The little tree felt a profound sense of satisfaction as he looked upon the glowing spectacle he had become. He firmly believed that this magnificent time would never end and that his future would remain bright. The sparkling lights cast intricate patterns across his branches, making him feel truly valuable and admired. He forgot entirely about the quiet forest, the birds, and the open sky that had once formed his entire world. In that dazzling room, surrounded by warmth and celebration, he assumed his ultimate purpose had finally been fulfilled.

When morning finally arrived, bringing a pale, cold light through the tall windows, the festive atmosphere vanished instantly. The brilliant electric lights were switched off, and the children ran out of the room to play elsewhere. Servants and family members came back to the grand room to strip the various ornaments from his branches. They pulled down the decorations without the slightest care, snapping a few tender twigs in their haste. The tree felt a sudden, hollow emptiness as his decorative burden was rudely removed piece by piece. No one paid any attention to him anymore, treating him merely as an inconvenient object to be cleared away.

Without warning, strong hands grabbed his trunk and dragged him roughly down the stairs into a dark, dusty basement room. The contrast between the dazzling ballroom upstairs and the dismal shadows below struck him with brutal force. He sat entirely alone in the cold, uninviting space, surrounded by discarded boxes and forgotten furniture. The silence of the basement felt heavy and suffocating compared to the music he had heard just hours before. A bitter realization began to form in his mind as the magnitude of his foolishness became clear.

Sitting in the dark shadows, the little tree thought about the warm light and the gentle wind of the distant forest. He remembered the birds that used to sing to him and the sun that had warmed his needles every afternoon. He realized with profound regret that he should have loved every simple day while he still lived there. Those ordinary moments of quiet growth, which he had once dismissed as worthless, now seemed like paradise lost. No magic awaited him down here; there was only the cold concrete floor and the smell of damp earth. He understood too late that happiness cannot be found by rushing toward an uncertain tomorrow.

Days blurred into a monotonous, freezing blur within the confines of the gloomy basement. His once-vibrant green needles began to turn a dull, sickly yellow, losing their moisture in the dry air. He had no water, no sunlight, and no pleasant company to distract him from his steady physical decline. Every hour felt longer than the last as he replayed the mistakes of his brief existence in his mind. The grand future he had desired so desperately had lasted for only a single fleeting night. Now, nothing remained of his glorious ambitions except the quiet ticking of time.

Men eventually came back down the stairs to drag the dry, faded tree out into the open yard. They hauled him roughly across the stone floor and laid him down flat on the cold grass under the bright sky. The midday sun beat down upon his brittle branches, but it brought no comfort to his withered form. He was no longer the proud, straight sapling that the woodsmen had chosen with such deliberate care. Stripped of his dignity, he lay discarded among the weeds near the back fence of the house. The contrast between his past hopes and his present ruin was absolute and complete.

Children from the house soon ran outside into the yard to play games around the abandoned tree. They paid no attention to his sad condition, treating his lifeless frame simply as another obstacle in their yard. Several of them jumped boldly upon his dry branches, snapping the brittle wood into many small, useless pieces. The little tree offered no resistance, feeling only the dull ache of physical destruction following his emotional collapse. He looked up at the vast blue sky one last time before his story finally reached its inevitable conclusion. He understood with perfect clarity that focusing exclusively on the future had completely destroyed his happiness.

If he had possessed the wisdom to appreciate the present, his fate might have been entirely different. He would have lived out a long, peaceful life among his towering companions in the deep, green forest. The gentle rain would have nourished his roots, and the morning breeze would have danced through his leaves for decades. Instead, blinded by ambition, he had traded a lifetime of quiet contentment for a single night of artificial glory. As the final twig snapped beneath the children running across the grass, his consciousness slowly faded away. The wind whispered softly through the remaining weeds, paying a quiet final tribute to the fallen fir tree.
